text:
maya: Quick sync — we should lock acceptance criteria for eval-triggered alerts that feed Optimize toolkit recommendations (batching/caching/quantization). Who's free?

tom: I can take this. main questions: which eval signals do we treat as hard vs advisory? e.g., perplexity drift vs hallucination rate.

elena: +1. my vote: hallucination/regression on golden prompts = hard (auto-fallback), throughput/latency degradation = advisory (recommend batched/quant variants).

sam: We need to map signals to concrete actions: 1) recommend different batching policy, 2) suggest caching prefixes, 3) suggest quantization tier (fp16/q4/qat). Also need rollout gating.

maya: Good. Let's propose tiers: SEVERE -> automatic fallback to verified model variant, CRITICAL -> page on-call + canary rollback, WARNING -> Optimizer suggestion only + in-console banner.

jordan: For pilots, propose starting with two customers: one high-throughput cohort (mobile chat) and one high-accuracy cohort (docs assistant). Want real signal coverage.

elena: For signal definitions: hallucination rate = % of eval prompts with F1 < 0.6 on golden spans; quality regression = avg BLEU/ROUGE drop > 3 pts; latency p95 up 30% over baseline. Anything else?

tom: Add token-efficiency regressions (tokens per useful token) and response truncation incidents. Both map well to quantization guidance.

maya: Nice. What about the alert payload shape so ops/Optimize can consume it? Minimal fields: signal, severity, metric_value, baseline, affected_model, recommended_action, confidence.

sam: Agree. Example payload: 
```json
{
  "signal": "hallucination_rate",
  "severity": "severe",
  "metric_value": "0.27",
  "baseline": "0.06",
  "affected_model": "redwood-open-13b-v1",
  "recommended_action": "fallback: redwood-open-13b-v1-safe, suggest: quant=q4_0, cache: enable_prefix",
  "confidence": "0.92"
}
```

jordan: Need to ensure we include prompt-set id + representative prompt examples for triage. Also include time window and sample ids for replay.

elena: Ops constraint: automatic fallback is only allowed for hosted and dedicated w/rollback OK. Private deployments should only get advisory recommendations unless enterprise config opts in.

tom: Right, add tenant capability flag in payload: supports_auto_fallback = true/false.

maya: Launch criteria draft: 1) alert generation stable for 2 weeks on pilot traffic, 2) false positive rate < 15% for SEVERE/CRITICAL, 3) runbook + canary rollback tested, 4) Optimize UI accepts and displays recommendations with A/B opt-in.

sam: For UX, we should surface a one-click apply for non-private tenants that toggles recommended batching/quant profiles. Also an explain link showing rationale & representative prompts.

jordan: Can we bundle a small simulation tool that estimates cost delta when applying quant/batch recommendations? customers will ask.

elena: Yes, Optimize already has econ heuristics — add a lightweight estimate endpoint that returns expected tokens/sec, unit cost delta, and expected quality delta band. Mark as experimental.

maya: Responsibilities: tom -> proto payload and hook from eval pipeline (1 week), sam -> catalog of actions + CLI/apply flow (2 weeks), elena -> severity definitions, runbooks, pilot selection (1 week), jordan -> pilot customers + acceptance criteria conversation (this week).

ci-bot: Deploy check: proto webhook endpoint created at /hooks/eval-alerts/proto (staging). Tests: 3 failing, 5 passing.

maya: Great. Action items and owners noted. Next sync Thursday 11am PT. If anyone disagrees with severity mapping above speak now or during prep doc review. :eyes:

tom: Quick note — we should add a toggle for auto-quantize only at low-confidence recommendations, to avoid regressions. i'll draft threshold heuristics.

elena: +1. also include an opt-out policy per-route.

maya: Thanks all — I'll open the spec PR with the payload + acceptance checklist after this. :thumbsup:
